title: Large-scale Asymmetries in the Transitional Disks of SAO 206462 and SR 21
question: What is the large-scale structure of the dust emission in the transitional disks of SAO 206462 and SR 21, and are the asymmetries consistent with vortex-like features?

data.sensitivity: Continuum RMS 0.0020 (SAO 206462) and 0.0011 (SR 21) Jy/beam; line RMS 0.11 and 0.07 Jy/beam per 0.5 km/s channel

what.value: H-band polarized intensity images of SAO 206462 and SR 21

evidence.quote: we present polarized intensity maps at H-band of both disks (cite: 2012Muto; 2013ApJ...767...10F)

external_data.citation: Muto et al. 2012 (cite: 2012Muto); Follette et al. 2013 (cite: 2013ApJ...767...10F)

what.value: Dust surface density at cavity edge ~0.1 g cm^-2 from 850 um observations

evidence.quote: constrained the surface density at the edge of the cavity to be $\Sigma_{dust}\sim0.1\:\textrm{gm~cm}^{-2}$ for both SAO 206462 and SR 21

recipe.goal: Image continuum and CO moment maps
recipe.method: Visibilities calibrated and imaged in CASA with Briggs weighting; CO moment 0 and 1 maps made

recipe.goal: Estimate optical depth and brightness temperature
recipe.method: Brightness temperature computed without Rayleigh-Jeans approximation; optical depth from literature surface density and opacity

recipe.goal: Fit ring and ring+vortex models to visibilities
recipe.method: Gaussian radial ring and Lyra & Lin vortex (Gaussian in r and theta) Fourier transformed and sampled at observed uv-positions; chi^2 minimized; PA fixed from CO moment 1; center and inclination free
key_parameters: SR 21 ring+vortex inclination fixed to 15 deg
assumptions: Ring emission axisymmetric; PA fixed to 62 deg (SAO 206462) and 16 deg (SR 21)

recipe.method: Convert vortex flux to mass; use vortex aspect ratio and Stokes number to infer turbulent velocity
assumptions: T=35 K, gas-to-dust 100, kappa=10 cm^2/g at 450 um for mass
a=1 mm, rho_s=1 g/cm3, Sigma=10 g/cm2, St~1e-2; gas T=50 K for sound speed

answer_key.quantity: Reduced chi^2 ring vs ring+vortex, SAO 206462
Reduced chi^2 ring vs ring+vortex, SR 21

evidence.quote: The vortex encompasses 15% of the total flux density for SAO 206462 and 28% for SR 21.
The flux density in the asymmetry corresponds to a mass (dust+gas) of $\sim2\:M_{\textrm{Jup}}$ for both SAO 206462 and SR 21
turbulent velocities of about $90\:\textrm{m~s}^{-1}$ and $68\:\textrm{m~s}^{-1}$ respectively
$T_b\sim30$ K for SAO 206462, and $T_b\sim35$ K for SR 21

not_stated_but_needed: Self-calibration solution intervals and reference antenna
Cell size, image size, deconvolver and masking
MCMC walkers, steps, burn-in, priors and parameter bounds
Flux calibrator model for Titan and flux uncertainty
How the moment maps were made (channel range, clip)
score_reason: Public Cycle 0 data and a simple model with a table of results, but calibration, self-cal and MCMC details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, the model is simple and results are numeric, though some details must be guessed.
